citation.title: Effects of different positive end-expiratory pressure titration strategies on mechanical power during ultraprotective ventilation in ARDS patients treated with veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: A prospective interventional study

provenance.quote: Exclusion criteria for the study were age younger than 18 years, and end-stage chronic cardiopulmonary failure.
All patients were ventilated with an Engström Carescape™ R860 ventilator (GE Healthcare, Munich, Germany) in a volume-controlled mode with a VT of 3 mL/kg predicted body weight
during the first three days of V–V ECMO treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) of the Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine, University Medical Centre Mannheim

Another dynamic recruitment maneuver was performed prior to ventilation with PEEP targeting an end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure of 0 cm H2O (PEEPPtpexp) and respiratory mechanics and hemodynamics were recorded.
Twenty patients with severe ARDS treated with V–V ECMO were included in the analysis.
This prospective interventional study was conducted as part of a multipurpose study [3]

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: ards_only: all 20 enrolled with severe ARDS per Berlin definition. obese_population: mean BMI 31.1 kg/m2 ≥ 30 per codebook rule. timing_subgroup unclear: timing is measured from ECMO start (mean 2 ± 1 days before study), not from intubation, ICU admission, or ARDS onset; the codebook reserves early/late labels for those reference events. ptp_target_subgroups: only the PEEPPtpexp condition targets end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure (0 cmH2O); the other two conditions are fixed PEEP and best compliance, which are not transpulmonary-pressure targets.

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: COHORTS.md suspects a mannheim_boesing cluster of boesing_2022 (n=40) and boesing_2024a (n=55) sharing a supine/prone esophageal-pressure-guided protocol, with boesing_2024b described as the VV-ECMO population. This report does not match that description: it is an n=20 VV-ECMO study (all patients on V–V ECMO, no prone positioning protocol), registered DRKS00013967 (registered 02/09/2018), ethics 2016-601 N-MA, University Medical Centre Mannheim. The prone-positioning study by the same group is cited here as reference [17] (Boesing C et al., Crit Care 2022;26:82), a separate publication and apparently a separate protocol. The COHORTS.md description of boesing_2024a (n=55, supine/prone protocol) appears inconsistent with the actual content of this PDF; the cluster assignment needs adjudication against the other Boesing records. Compared: trial registration (DRKS00013967, this paper), population (VV-ECMO, n=20), and the cited 2022 prone study as a distinct reference.
unclear_items: extraction_flags.cohort_id / overlap: COHORTS.md's description of boesing_2024a (n=55, supine/prone protocol) does not match this report (n=20, VV-ECMO); cohort clustering among boesing_2022/2024a/2024b needs adjudication.
intervention.ptp_computation.method: coded absolute_pes_subtraction, but the paper only says formulas are 'detailed in the Supplement'; the Supplement was not provided.

intervention.balloon_calibration.method: filling volume was manufacturer-recommended (2 mL air) with validity checked by an occlusion ratio of 0.8–1.2; the enum does not cleanly cover this combination, so manufacturer_recommended_volume was coded with the occlusion check in position_verification.
design.randomised: coded false because the paper states the sequence of PEEP titration strategies was not randomized; no other randomisation is described.
arms[peep_ptpexp].peep_applied_cmh2o dispersion: abstract reports 17.3 ± 4.0 cmH2O but Table 2 reports 17.3 ± 4.7 cmH2O; Table 2 value recorded, discrepancy flagged.
feasibility.n_placement_attempted / n_placement_successful: esophageal pressure was measured in all 20 patients but placement success is not explicitly reported; left null rather than derived.
population.covid19_population: not_reported; cause-of-ARDS breakdown lists only bacterial pneumonia, influenza pneumonia, and non-pulmonary sepsis.
outcomes: ICU mortality (7/20, 35%) is reported only in Table 1 as a cohort-level variable and has no per-condition data; recorded in population.additional_baseline rather than as an outcome entry.
subgroup_flags.timing_subgroup: coded unclear because the reference event is ECMO start, not one of the codebook's qualifying events.

extraction_flags.general_notes: Correlations reported: ΔPEEP vs ΔMechanical Power (rho = 0.929, r2 = 0.893, p < 0.001); MP vs lung stress (rho = 0.659, r2 = 0.441, p < 0.001); MP vs MPtp (rho = 0.890, r2 = 0.820, p < 0.001) — these are across-strategy correlations, not condition contrasts, so they are not recorded as paired_effects. The study was conducted as part of a multipurpose study (reference [3], Graf PT et al., J Intensive Care 2022) — potential cohort overlap with that report should be checked if it enters the review. No omnibus ANOVA p-values are printed per variable; Table 2 reports only Holm-Sidak-adjusted pairwise p-values. ECMO blood-flow and gas-flow rates did not differ between strategies (Table S1, Supplement not provided).
